text: Here is a simple co-pilot agent that helps me prepare leadership updates. I've configured how I want that work done, what to focus on, what to avoid, and how to structure the results. So I can reuse the assistant instead of rebuilding the prompt every single time I need to use it. But I am still operating the workflow. I'm gathering the meeting notes, the project updates, the metrics, then I start the process, and then I decide what happens with the results. So what changes when I move this into co-pilot studio? So if like me you have an existing co-pilot agent, I can take that existing agent and copy it into co-pilot studio. To do that I want to click the three dots, then click edit, more options, and copy to co-pilot studio. If you don't see this option you likely don't have a co-pilot studio license. Now on this screen Microsoft will show me what it will and will not transfer. Most of the core agent setup comes with me including the name, the icon, the description, the instructions, the suggested prompts, the enterprise knowledge, and supported SharePoint and website sources. But some things do not transfer automatically like uploaded files, teams and outlook knowledge sources, sharing settings, image generation settings, and actions. That said I'm going to click here on get started. Okay and now I can continue and select the power platform environment where I want the agent to live. So that environment needs a dataverse database and the available options will depend on how your organization has configured co-pilot studio. Then I can click on create and co-pilot studio now saves the new version of my agents. Now even with this co-pilot studio agents the core job of writing leadership updates is still the same and the instructions still cover what matters, what to avoid, and how the output should be structured. But now I can start adding capabilities around that intelligence. So let's start with the information. So right now again I'm gathering those inputs manually. In co-pilot studio I can connect the agent to approved sources. So I go to knowledge, then SharePoint, and then add a data source that the agent can access and update itself with. That changes the workflow in a very practical way. So instead of gathering information for AI to process the system can now retrieve it itself and then process it. This is a relatively low consequence capability because the agent is just retrieving information and not changing anything. So I can usually let it do that without asking me every time. The next step is tools. So a tool lets the agent do more than produce an answer. It might retrieve information from another system. It could create or update something or it could run a predefined workflow. So for example once this leadership update is ready I could add a Microsoft Teams tool that lets the agent post a message to the leadership channel announcing that our meeting agenda is ready for review. The tools that you see here again depend on your company setup and access and some require you to set up a connection first. But in my case instead of the workflow ending with the draft that I need to copy somewhere else because of this connector I can now ask something like create this week's leadership update and post it to the leadership channel. The agent can then use its instructions and the connected information to create the updates and then use the Teams tool to publish the results. Now the AI is no longer only helping me create an output but carry a defined step of the workflow forward in another system. Now many steps in processes like these require judgment while others should be very predictable and co-pilots to support both. So inside tools I can click on workflows and then I can choose or create the agent flow that I need. So here I can tell the AI to always run a process if a condition is met but I can also tell it to ask me or others for inputs before proceeding by choosing plus, add an action, human review and then request information and then filling out the message and who should receive it. I can also connect specialist agents. So for example I could connect a finance update agent that has its own instructions and access to the information needed to prepare the financial section. My leadership agent can then use the specialist when it needs it rather than trying to make one enormous agent that does everything. So all of what we just went through that is the shift that co-pilot studio makes possible. We go from one reusable assistant toward a system that can get information, use tools and delegate parts of the work. So now the useful question for us becomes which parts of this workflow could the system carry forward for me and where do I still want a human involved?
